items.title: 全生态物理 AI 落地，小米的主场攻防战

excerpt_i18n.en: Over the past three years, rapid advances in large models have first played out in the digital world. Text, images, code, and video can all be converted into data, from which models learn patterns through massive pre-training before performing comprehension, reasoning, and generation. Yet the tasks and scenarios the digital world can cover are ultimately limited. If AI is to further expand its industrial value, it must move from information processing into the real world, beginning to understand the environment and interact with the physical world. If this wave of AI is divided into two phases, the first half was a contest over models; competition in the second half is increasingly shifting toward the deployment of physical AI. At IFA, this year's largest consumer electronics and future technology exhibition, Leiphone clearly sensed that AI is moving beyond content generation and digital tasks into the physical world. The show featured a dedicated "World of AI & Future of Tech" agenda, spotlighting the latest advances in robotics, AI wearables, and smart homes, with the largest number of humanoid robots on display of any edition to date. Clearly, no company wants to miss the opportunity presented by physical AI, the most imaginative industrial prospect since mobile internet. Xiaomi, as the world's first tech company to achieve full "Human x Car x Home" ecosystem deployment in physical AI, unsurprisingly drew widespread attention from overseas consumers at IFA this year. items.title: How Intuit built an agentic disaster recovery assistant with Amazon Bedrock
